To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the role of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in chronic glutamate toxicity depends on the cell type.
astrocytic phospholipoase A2 contributes significantly to neuronal glutamate cytotoxicity in neuron-astro-cyte co-cultures.
astrocytic phospholippase A2 contributes neuronal glutamate toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of astrocytic PLA activity in glutamate-induced neuronal toxicity.
the mechanism of astrocytic PLA activity in neuronal glutamate toxicity.
the mechanisms of astrocytic PLA activity, which contributes to neuronal toxicity induced by chronic glutamate exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
astrocytic phospholipoase A2 contributes neuronal glutamate toxicity by generating arachidonic acid, and this process is mediated by reactive oxygen species.
astrocytic 5-LO, 12-LO and COX activity contribute to the neuronal glutamate toxicity, and that astrocytic cPLA2 and sPLA2 contribute to the glutamate toxicity via a 5-LO and/or 12-LO pathway.

astrocytic cPLA2 and sPLA2V, which are involved in the generation of 15-HETE from AA, are responsible for neuronal glutamate toxicity, whereas astrocytic COX and neuronal PLA2 are responsible for neuronal survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glutamate toxicity is enhanced in co-cultured neurons by astrocytic PLA activity and the toxicity is reduced by astrocytic COX activity.
astrocytic phospholippase A2 activity increases neuronal vulnerability to glutamate toxicity by enhancing neuronal glutamate release and by reducing astrocytic glutathione production.
astrocytes increase neuronal sensitivity to glutamate toxicity by enhancing the production of reactive oxygen species via PLA2 and reducing the production of H2O2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
astrocytic phospholipoase A2 contributes significantly to neuronal glutamate excitotoxicity.
astrocytes contribute to neuronal glutamate cytotoxicity by enhancing PLA2 activity.
astrocytic phospholipoase A2 (PA2) activity contributes to the neuronal glutamate toxicity.
